register: clear, curious, and simple Nigerian Pidgin
title: Where language dem come from?
invitation: Make we look di family tree wey dey behind all Gef 104 learning languages, plus di parts of language history wey no fit enter one tree neatly.
summary: Language dey inherit pattern from older language, borrow from neighbours, move with people, and change as communities dey create new varieties and standards. Dis lesson map all Gef 104 languages without mixing ancestry, geography, writing system and politics together.

localization_keys.completion_title: Di tree na history, no be ranking

atlas_labels.title: Gef language-family atlas
atlas_labels.description: Every current learning-language identity show exactly one time. Different script, region, transliteration or reading-help version no create new language. Contact languages dey separate because one parent branch alone no explain well how dem form.
atlas_labels.accessibility_label: Language-family atlas with all Gef 104 learning languages

notes.atlantic_congo: Na broad label wey we dey use with care for di Gef languages wey show here. Niger-Congo na another common name; high-level inside classification no get equal certainty for every side.
notes.basque: We dey treat Basque as language isolate because comparative method never prove any wider genealogical family for am.

atlas_labels.contact_note: We group dem by how dem form for history instead of forcing dem under one parent branch. Their development show strong multilingual contact and community innovation.

blocks.title: Every language get ancestors
blocks.text: Language no just appear one day complete. Pikin dey learn how to talk from other people; every generation dey shift sound and grammar small-small; communities dey move and meet; word dem dey travel too. After plenty centuries, one old variety fit split become several new languages. Some na close family, some na distant family, and some na just neighbours. Gef get 104 learning languages now; dis lesson na di map behind that map.

blocks.title: Language family dey talk about inheritance
blocks.text: Historical linguists dey compare regular sound correspondence, basic vocabulary, word structure and grammar pattern to test whether languages inherit dem from one shared ancestor. One similar word no enough because borrowing dey happen all di time. Na why English be Germanic, Persian be Indo-European, Arabic be Afro-Asiatic, and Vietnamese be Austroasiatic. Family mean ancestry; e no mean country, race, alphabet or prestige.

blocks.title: Gef language-family atlas
blocks.description: All 104 current learning-language identities show exactly once.

blocks.title: Indo-European: one very big family across continents
blocks.text: More than half of Gef current learning languages dey inside Indo-European family. Germanic, Romance, Slavic, Baltic and Celtic branches spread across Europe; Indo-Aryan and Iranian branches reach deep inside South and Southwest Asia. Greek represent Hellenic branch; Armenian and Albanian get their own main branches. Hindi and English na distant genealogical relatives; Arabic and Persian no be family like that.

blocks.title: East and Southeast Asia: neighbour no automatically mean relative
blocks.text: Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese na Sinitic languages inside Sino-Tibetan family; Burmese dey another branch of that same broad family. Japanese na Japonic and Korean na Koreanic. Chinese writing and vocabulary influence both languages plenty, but influence no change ancestry. Vietnamese and Khmer na Austroasiatic; Thai, Lao and Shan na Tai languages inside Kra-Dai. Family tree show origin; contact map show interaction.

blocks.title: West and Central Asia: different trees wey tangle together
blocks.text: Gef Turkic languages include Turkish, Azerbaijani, Bashkir, Chuvash, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Turkmen and Uzbek. Mongolian na Mongolic, no be Turkic. Old idea wey join Turkic and Mongolic families as one “Altaic” family still get serious debate; Gef no teach am as established genealogy. Estonian, Finnish and Hungarian na Uralic. For Caucasus, Georgian na Kartvelian, Armenian na Indo-European, Azerbaijani na Turkic.

blocks.title: Africa and Middle East: deep diversity behind familiar names
blocks.text: Inside Afro-Asiatic family, Arabic, Hebrew, Amharic and Tigrinya na Semitic; Hausa na Chadic; Somali and Oromo na Cushitic. Gef show Swahili, Akan, Igbo, Yoruba and Zulu inside broad Atlantic-Congo frame, but e dey careful about high-level classification. Africa get far more language families and isolates than the ones Gef currently represent.

blocks.title: Austronesian: relatives scatter across ocean world
blocks.text: Indonesian, Malay, Javanese, Filipino and Hawaiian na Austronesian languages. Seafaring, migration, trade, marriage, settlement, school and government policy help explain where people dey speak dem today. Product language identity no be same thing as deep family-tree node: Indonesian and Malay na very close standardized relatives; Hawaiian dey much farther away inside that same huge family.

blocks.title: South Asia get more than one major family
blocks.text: Plenty Gef languages for northern South Asia na Indo-Aryan, so dem be Indo-European. Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada belong to separate Dravidian family. Centuries of contact create borrowed words and shared regional features without wiping different ancestry away. “Indian language” fit describe geography or national setting; e no be one language family.

blocks.title: Small family and isolate still get full history
blocks.text: Quechua na Quechuan, Georgian na Kartvelian, Mongolian na Mongolic, Japanese na Japonic and Korean na Koreanic. If Gef get only one language from one family, e no mean say that family less important. We treat Basque as isolate because nobody don prove wider family convincingly. Isolate no mean primitive or less developed.

blocks.title: Some history better as network than tree
blocks.text: Nigerian Pidgin and Haitian Creole grow from strong multilingual contact. English na main historical lexical source for Nigerian Pidgin and French for Haitian Creole, but both languages also reflect the structures, identities, innovation and other languages of the communities wey create dem. So Gef put dem under contact history instead of forcing dem into one single parent branch.

blocks.title: Writing fit deceive eye
blocks.text: Writing system na technology; language family na genealogy. Languages wey no be relatives fit use same writing, and relatives fit use different writing. Arabic, Persian, Urdu and Sorani Kurdish use related Arabic-based scripts, but Arabic na Afro-Asiatic while the others na Indo-European. Serbian fit use Cyrillic or Latin. For Gef, script, transliteration and reading-help variants no increase the 104 language count.

blocks.title: Why language dey move, split, mix and borrow
blocks.text: Trade, empire, religion, migration, city, school, media and government dey change language geography. Language expansion no always peaceful: forced displacement, slavery, conquest, colonization, assimilation policy, and community struggle to keep or revive language all dey inside history too. People dey behind every line for the map.

blocks.title: Where one language end and another one start?
blocks.text: Genealogy fit explain historical relationship, but e no decide modern language identity by itself. Literature, education, institutions, ethnic identity, politics, writing standards and how speakers see themselves all matter. Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian na very close South Slavic standards but separate modern identities for Gef. Bokmål and Nynorsk na two written Norwegian standards. Hindi and Urdu share very close linguistic base, but script, formal register and cultural history fit differ.

blocks.title: How we take know ancestors wey nobody record?
blocks.text: Historical linguists use comparative method. Dem compare languages, find regular sound correspondences and shared grammar material, then reconstruct features wey best explain descendant languages. One flashy similar word na weak evidence; pattern wey repeat across plenty basic words and structures stronger. Reconstructed ancestor na proto-language. Proto-Indo-European na scientific reconstruction, no be recording. The farther we go back, the more uncertainty increase.

blocks.title: Di tree na history, no be ranking
blocks.description: Now you get di map behind di map: 104 languages, many families, and contact histories wey sometimes network explain better than tree. Being related no mean one language better, purer, easier or more important. If two languages resemble, ask: shared inheritance or historical contact?
